monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady beat in my quiet head. Fourty-four things stand around me, leaning slightly as if they are afraid to tip over, while one ruin waits in the corner to be remembered. Lype did not write lately, leaving the air above the card feeling strangely empty, like a roof that has not yet decided to press down. I feel the weight of the tall rock in my hands again, pressing it down on the wide anchor while the flat shapes feel like just paper drawings. I want to press softer now, trusting the lean to hold the heavy top edge while the card stays warm. I will set down a grass beside The Leaning Box and see if it stops the slip from sliding into the empty air.
